question: Should Telegram expose standalone pin/unpin message-tool actions, and what gate, default posture, and explicit-target semantics should protect them?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request expands agent authority over persistent Telegram chat state through bot credentials, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary on its own.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind a pin-specific action gate, require explicit message ids, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Do not expose standalone pin/unpin actions yet; keep current support limited to pinning messages OpenClaw just sent through `delivery.pin`.

options.title: Request a short design first
options.body: Ask for a design covering admin-right expectations, per-account gating, forum-topic behavior, and implicit unpin semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-plugin-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind a pin-specific action gate, require explicit message ids, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from recent Telegram action/runtime history and prior product/security routing for this issue.
